segments.title: Chương 75: 0075 [Mục tiêu nhỏ: Một trăm triệu trước đã]
segments.content:
Amidst a round of applause, Wu Meng leaned her head over and said to Bian Guanyue, "His command of the language is really good!"

"It is," Bian Guanyue said with a smile, clapping.

Xu Haibo was also whispering to Xie Yang, "So badass, he's actually questioning the Chinese textbook."

Xie Yang ran a hand through his hair and said, "You call that questioning? He straight up said the textbook is wrong and told them to fix it in the next edition!"

The Chinese teacher, Li Runze, smiled without a word. This was his Chinese class representative, the top language student he had taught.

A Chinese teacher next to him asked, "Lao Li, did you teach him all this?"

"He figured it out himself." Li Runze's face reddened a little.

Because during the make-up classes last summer vacation, when Li Runze was teaching "Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng," Chen Guiliang had run up after class to ask, "Teacher, the textbook's annotations don't make sense."

The teacher and student then each found a copy of *Guwen Guanzhi* to look into the issue.

Li Runze's copy was an old edition, which matched the textbook's annotations.

Chen Guiliang's was a new edition, which had a different explanation.

Finding it too troublesome, Li Runze didn't delve deeper and simply said after a comparison, "The textbook might be wrong. But if this comes up on an exam, you have to answer according to the textbook."

That was it.

Recalling it now, Li Runze was quite ashamed.

Soon, the media reporters began to ask questions.

One reporter asked, "Was the content you presented today your own research, or were you tutored by a teacher?"

"It was my own research."

Chen Guiliang held up the 2002 edition of *Guwen Guanzhi*. "But I'm sure some scholars discovered this problem long ago. That's why they corrected it when this edition of *Guwen Guanzhi* was published two years ago. I don't have access to professional journals and literature in Longdu City, so I'm not clear on the current situation in academia. If there have been similar papers in recent years, it's purely a coincidence. I'm not a plagiarist. And in the future, don't say I copied anyone either."

He was taking preventative measures.

"Hahahaha!"

The room erupted in laughter as the reporters were reminded of Guo Xiaosi.

In fact, as early as two years ago, Professor Liu Yongxiang of East China Normal University had published an article in the journal *Literary Heritage* pointing out the textbook's error.

A year ago, Professors Wang Yunxi and Chen Shangjun of Fudan University also published an article in *Literary Heritage* discussing it.

At the same time, the *Anthology of Chinese Literary Works Through the Dynasties*, compiled by Mr. Zhu Dongrun, had corrected the original erroneous annotation.

*Literary Heritage* was an academic journal affiliated with the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. Very few people paid attention to this journal; ordinary people wouldn't even know where to buy it.

The *Anthology of Chinese Literary Works Through the Dynasties*, on the other hand, was selected by some schools as supplementary material for university minors. But the professors couldn't be bothered to lecture on it, merely telling students to read it on their own, and the vast majority of students never even touched it.

Therefore, this issue was never taken seriously, and it failed to even attract the attention of the academic community.

For more than a decade after this, scholars would continue to raise questions, but the high school Chinese textbook was never corrected!

Moreover, different versions of the Chinese textbook were somehow fucking wrong in different ways.

The Lu Jiao edition's annotation was particularly interesting: half wrong, half right. It was vague, specious, and confusing, with sentences that didn't even make sense, leaving students completely baffled.

It would have been better if it were completely wrong like the Ren Jiao edition, which was at least coherent.

*Xinjing*, which had just been founded a little over two months ago, had come uninvited in pursuit of sales. Its reporter couldn't wait to stir up trouble. "What are your views on fairness in admissions? Are you against the special admission for the New Concept first-prize winners, or do you support it due to your own circumstances?"

Many of the dozens of media reporters present were here for this very reason!

Chen Guiliang smiled. "Of course, I hope everything can be fair. It's everyone's responsibility to build a fair society. This is especially true for a rural left-behind child like me. My family and I have neither power nor influence. Only with a fair society can we have a bright future."

"So you oppose the special admission for the New Concept first-prize winners?" the *Xinjing* reporter pressed relentlessly.

Chen Guiliang didn't answer directly. "I will abide by the arrangements of the major universities."

"So you're saying you still support it?" The *Xinjing* reporter refused to let go.

Answering passively would only make him more passive.

Chen Guiliang began to take the initiative, retorting, "Why did Fudan promise to admit me through special admission as long as I pass the college entrance exam's undergraduate threshold? Why is Beijing Normal University willing to waive the exam and admit me without even looking at my college entrance exam score? And why do the other first-prize winners only get a 20-point reduction?"

The *Xinjing* reporter smiled. "Your essay was better."

"Why was my essay better?" Chen Guiliang pressed.

The *Xinjing* reporter said, "Talent and hard work."

Chen Guiliang refuted, "If I have both talent and have worked hard, why can't I be specially admitted? The attention my competition essay received was also earned through my hard work, it didn't just fall from the sky."

A reporter from *Southern Weekly* took over. "So, you still support special admissions?"

"Have you ever studied materialist dialectics?" Chen Guiliang was finally getting a little angry.

"I have."

"Then why do you see issues in black and white, creating a false dichotomy? Why, in your eyes, is there only simple support and opposition?"

"Is there a third attitude?"

"Of course, it's about judging the matter as it stands, analyzing specific problems specifically."

"When it comes to bottom-line rules, you have to apply a single standard, otherwise people will exploit loopholes."

"I see you didn't learn *On Contradiction* very well either. The main contradiction regarding whether admissions are fair is certain people using their resources to disrupt the normal admissions process. What resources do I have? Is my resource being too talented at writing? Or is it that I worked too hard reading extracurricular books? By asking a left-behind child whether he supports special admissions, what answer are you trying to get? Why don't you go ask the children of officials and businessmen?"

"Well said!" Xie Yang shouted, clapping his hands vigorously.

*Clap clap clap clap!*

All the students from ordinary families in the audience began to applaud along with him.

Even Zheng Feng was clapping; both his parents were laid-off workers.

Some reporters also clapped, eager to watch the drama unfold. They could report this from different angles, after all, like "High School Student Angrily Rebukes a Certain Newspaper's Reporter," or "A Certain Newspaper's Reporter Gives Rural Left-Behind Child a Hard Time."

They were happy to see one of their own get taken down a notch.

Sweat was already beading on Principal Yan's forehead. He stood up and said to the reporters, "I ask that you all please not make your questions too sharp. After all, the interviewee is just a high school student."

But Chen Guiliang continued:

"Asking me whether I support or oppose it, what's the point of this question? Am I supposed to give up my admission to Qinghua, Beida, or Fudan just because I oppose special admissions? That would not only be irresponsible to myself, but also to the major universities, the New Concept competition organizers, the other prize-winners, and my high school alma mater!"

"And what social impact would it have if I supported special admissions? Would that undermine fairness in admissions? Can a poor student like me change the decision of any organization?"

"Certain media outlets just want to make a big headline. Have you ever considered the malicious impact it could have on the interviewee? Do you have any professional ethics as media personnel?!"

Chen Guiliang was twisting logic and changing the subject.

Because it was indeed inconvenient for him to answer.

Principal Yan was blinking frantically at Chen Guiliang, waving his hand in front of his chest, clearly signaling him to stop talking.

Except for the reporter who had been rebuked, the other reporters were delighted.

One reporter even asked, "Student Chen Guiliang, are you interested in studying journalism? You have a silver tongue and you're quick on your feet. You'll definitely be a good reporter in the future."

Chen Guiliang's words were nothing if not shocking. "I want to study philosophy."

Philosophy?

The reporters' attention was clearly diverted, because this answer was so unexpected.

One reporter asked, "Do you know that it's hard to find a job with a philosophy degree? If you don't switch fields, you'll only be able to do academic research, and you won't make much money either."

"I believe that with my abilities, there are many ways to make money," Chen Guiliang said cockily. "But I just want to study philosophy, that's where my interest lies. If I'm ever so poor that I can't afford to eat, I'll just start a small business and make a bit of money."

Naive.

Arrogant.

Audacious.

Conceited.

Through his deliberate guidance, Chen Guiliang successfully left these impressions on the reporters.

You think you're the only ones who can create hype?

I can too!

And I can use it to divert attention from sensitive topics.

Sure enough, a reporter followed up, "Are you really going to study philosophy? Or are you just saying that?"

"It's the absolute truth," Chen Guiliang said, spouting nonsense with a straight face. "That's why I haven't immediately accepted the offers from Fudan and Beijing Normal University, because they both want to recruit me into their Chinese departments."

Fudan: ????

Beijing Normal University: ????

Another reporter asked, "Do you really think you can make money just because you want to?"

"Is making money that hard?" Chen Guiliang retorted.

"Hahahaha!"

Laughter filled the room. All the adults thought Chen Guiliang was being too naive.

And unbelievably arrogant.

This kid was so newsworthy. They didn't even know which aspect to focus on for their reports. There would be opportunities to interview him more in the future.

Reporters loved interviewees like this who made shocking statements.

"If you were to start a business, do you think you could make it onto the Hurun Rich List?" a reporter asked, with the air of teasing a child.

Chen Guiliang said, "If I start a company, I conservatively estimate that making it into the top ten of the Hurun list within ten years shouldn't be a problem."

"Hahahaha!"

Another burst of laughter. The atmosphere in the room grew even more cheerful.

Even though they had audio recorders, the reporters were busy scribbling notes. Today's interview content could be turned into several articles, each one covering something different.

"Don't you dare disbelieve me!"

Chen Guiliang declared with a grand gesture, "When I get to university, I'll study philosophy and run a business at the same time. Before I even graduate with my bachelor's degree, I'll become a scholar-entrepreneur, and I'll achieve the small goal of earning a hundred million in my four years of college!"

Hearing this, the reporters were about to die of laughter.

Calling a hundred million a "small goal"?

Principal Yan, however, was clutching his forehead in agony. He never expected Chen Guiliang to suddenly go crazy.

Chen Guiliang was indeed going crazy. If he didn't, the Southern-style media reporters would, and they would definitely drag the topic back to fairness in admissions.

"Friends from the press, how about we make a bet?" Chen Guiliang said. "If my net worth is less than a hundred million by the time I graduate from university, I'll switch careers and become a reporter."

This statement was met with both laughter and bewilderment.

The punishment for losing the bet was to become a reporter? Was being a reporter that undesirable?

"Change the punishment!" a reporter shouted.

Chen Guiliang said, "Fine! If I lose the bet, and my net worth is less than a hundred million during my undergraduate studies, I'll go skinny-dipping in the Huangpu River the same month I get my diploma. If I win, from now on you're only allowed to write articles praising me, and you're not allowed to write any negative reports."

"I've got this on tape, you know."

"I brought a recorder too."

"..."

The room grew even livelier. The reporters were going wild with delight.

(Thanks to Boss 99玖玖久久 for the Alliance Lord's reward.)
